assertions.description: navigator.keyboard.lock is a function — the Keyboard Lock call Chromium maps to the KEYBOARD_LOCK_REQUESTED scam-check trigger (desktop only; absent on Android).
Element.prototype.requestPointerLock is a function — the call Chromium maps to the POINTER_LOCK_REQUESTED trigger.
Element.prototype.requestFullscreen is a function — the call Chromium maps to the FULLSCREEN_API trigger.
Clipboard.prototype.writeText is a function — page-initiated copies are what the desktop CLIPBOARD_COPY_API trigger tokenises.
Notification.requestPermission is a function — showing its prompt is the NOTIFICATION_PERMISSION_PROMPT trigger.
HTMLElement.innerText omits display:none text — the scan reads the page's rendered inner text, so cloaked hidden copy is not part of what is sent.

assertions.description: The feature adds no web API: neither navigator nor the global object exposes a Safe Browsing / Enhanced Protection state or scam-check verdict a page could read.
assertions.test: !('safeBrowsing' in navigator) && !('SafeBrowsing' in globalThis) && !('scamDetection' in navigator)

assertions.description: For an Enhanced Safe Browsing desktop user, a high-confidence trigger can send the page's visible text to Safe Browsing's server-side Gemini model and Chrome shows its own interstitial on a scam verdict.
assertions.test: Not observable from a web page: requires an Enhanced Safe Browsing profile, a server request for an intelligent scan, and remaining daily quota (MaxIntelligentScansPerDayDesktop = 5); the verdict and interstitial are browser UI.
